You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:

CREATE TABLE continents (
    ContId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Continent TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE countries (
    CountryId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    CountryName TEXT,
    Continent INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (Continent) REFERENCES continents(ContId)
);

CREATE TABLE car_makers (
    Id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Maker TEXT,
    FullName TEXT,
    Country TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (Country) REFERENCES countries(CountryId)
);

CREATE TABLE model_list (
    ModelId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Maker INTEGER,
    Model TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Model),
    FOREIGN KEY (Maker) REFERENCES car_makers(Id)
);

CREATE TABLE car_names (
    MakeId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Model TEXT,
    Make TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (Model) REFERENCES model_list(Model)
);

CREATE TABLE cars_data (
    Id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    MPG TEXT,
    Cylinders INTEGER,
    Edispl REAL,
    Horsepower TEXT,
    Weight INTEGER,
    Accelerate REAL,
    Year INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (Id) REFERENCES car_names(MakeId)
);

When you have a final SQL query to present, always wrap it in a sql markdown code fence like this:

```sql
SELECT ...
```

This makes it easy to identify your answer. Only use one ```sql fence for your final query.

If by “old car makers” you mean makers with cars from early model years, this query summarizes each maker whose earliest car record is from 1975 or earlier:

```sql
SELECT
    cm.Maker,
    cm.FullName,
    co.CountryName,
    ct.Continent,
    MIN(cd.Year) AS earliest_year,
    MAX(cd.Year) AS latest_year,
    COUNT(*) AS total_car_records,
    SUM(CASE WHEN cd.Year <= 1975 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS old_car_records,
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN cd.MPG != '?' THEN CAST(cd.MPG AS REAL) END), 2) AS avg_mpg,
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN cd.Horsepower != '?' THEN CAST(cd.Horsepower AS REAL) END), 2) AS avg_horsepower,
    ROUND(AVG(cd.Weight), 2) AS avg_weight
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN model_list ml
    ON cm.Id = ml.Maker
JOIN car_names cn
    ON ml.Model = cn.Model
JOIN cars_data cd
    ON cn.MakeId = cd.Id
LEFT JOIN countries co
    ON cm.Country = co.CountryId
LEFT JOIN continents ct
    ON co.Continent = ct.ContId
GROUP BY
    cm.Id,
    cm.Maker,
    cm.FullName,
    co.CountryName,
    ct.Continent
HAVING MIN(cd.Year) <= 1975
ORDER BY
    earliest_year ASC,
    old_car_records DESC;
```
focus on car makers that made vehicles a long time ago

This focuses on car makers with the earliest recorded vehicles in the dataset, showing only makers whose first vehicle record is from 1975 or earlier:

```sql
SELECT
    cm.Maker,
    cm.FullName,
    co.CountryName,
    ct.Continent,
    MIN(cd.Year) AS first_recorded_year,
    COUNT(*) AS total_vehicle_records,
    SUM(CASE WHEN cd.Year <= 1975 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS old_vehicle_records
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN model_list ml
    ON cm.Id = ml.Maker
JOIN car_names cn
    ON ml.Model = cn.Model
JOIN cars_data cd
    ON cn.MakeId = cd.Id
LEFT JOIN countries co
    ON cm.Country = co.CountryId
LEFT JOIN continents ct
    ON co.Continent = ct.ContId
GROUP BY
    cm.Id,
    cm.Maker,
    cm.FullName,
    co.CountryName,
    ct.Continent
HAVING MIN(cd.Year) <= 1975
ORDER BY
    first_recorded_year ASC,
    old_vehicle_records DESC;
```
also want to check that some cars were made in 1970.

You can add a 1970-specific count and require at least one 1970 vehicle record:

```sql
SELECT
    cm.Maker,
    cm.FullName,
    co.CountryName,
    ct.Continent,
    MIN(cd.Year) AS first_recorded_year,
    COUNT(*) AS total_vehicle_records,
    SUM(CASE WHEN cd.Year <= 1975 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS old_vehicle_records,
    SUM(CASE WHEN cd.Year = 1970 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS vehicles_made_in_1970
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN model_list ml
    ON cm.Id = ml.Maker
JOIN car_names cn
    ON ml.Model = cn.Model
JOIN cars_data cd
    ON cn.MakeId = cd.Id
LEFT JOIN countries co
    ON cm.Country = co.CountryId
LEFT JOIN continents ct
    ON co.Continent = ct.ContId
GROUP BY
    cm.Id,
    cm.Maker,
    cm.FullName,
    co.CountryName,
    ct.Continent
HAVING
    MIN(cd.Year) <= 1975
    AND SUM(CASE WHEN cd.Year = 1970 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
    vehicles_made_in_1970 DESC,
    first_recorded_year ASC;
```
Also want to include the names of car makers that fit these criteria.

This includes the car maker names directly via `cm.Maker` and `cm.FullName`, while keeping the criteria that they have older vehicles and at least one vehicle from 1970:

```sql
SELECT
    cm.Maker AS maker_name,
    cm.FullName AS maker_full_name,
    co.CountryName,
    ct.Continent,
    MIN(cd.Year) AS first_recorded_year,
    COUNT(*) AS total_vehicle_records,
    SUM(CASE WHEN cd.Year <= 1975 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS old_vehicle_records,
    SUM(CASE WHEN cd.Year = 1970 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS vehicles_made_in_1970
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN model_list ml
    ON cm.Id = ml.Maker
JOIN car_names cn
    ON ml.Model = cn.Model
JOIN cars_data cd
    ON cn.MakeId = cd.Id
LEFT JOIN countries co
    ON cm.Country = co.CountryId
LEFT JOIN continents ct
    ON co.Continent = ct.ContId
GROUP BY
    cm.Id,
    cm.Maker,
    cm.FullName,
    co.CountryName,
    ct.Continent
HAVING
    MIN(cd.Year) <= 1975
    AND SUM(CASE WHEN cd.Year = 1970 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
    vehicles_made_in_1970 DESC,
    first_recorded_year ASC,
    maker_name ASC;
```
